text: Bouldering grades are a guide, not an exact measurement: height, reach and climbing style can change how a problem feels.
Clean climbing shoes improve friction and help to keep dirt away from the holds.
Brushing excess chalk from holds improves friction and leaves the boulder cleaner for the next climber.
A small amount of chalk is usually enough. Too much chalk can make holds feel worse rather than better.
Before climbing, check the landing zone for stones, gaps and branches and position the crash pads accordingly.
The main purpose of spotting is to guide a falling climber towards the crash pads, not to catch the climber.
Crash pads reduce impact, but they cannot remove every risk. A controlled descent remains the safest option.
A gradual warm-up prepares fingers, shoulders and the rest of the body for harder climbing.
Looking for a safe way down is part of checking a boulder before starting the climb.
Granite friction often feels different as temperature and humidity change during the day.
Granite can be demanding on the skin, so short breaks may help both performance and recovery.
Keeping noise low helps protect the atmosphere of the area and avoids disturbing wildlife and other visitors.
Take tape, food packaging and all other waste back with you, even if it was left by someone else.
Using existing paths limits erosion and reduces damage to the vegetation around the boulders.
Remove tick marks after climbing so that the rock remains clean and the next climber can solve the moves independently.
In this guide, a Project is a line that has not yet received a confirmed grade.
A flash means completing a boulder on the first attempt, even if the climber has already received information about the moves.
Climbers often call information about the movements and sequence of a problem beta.
The Fontainebleau scale uses numbers, letters and plus signs to describe increasing bouldering difficulty.
The same boulder can have several good solutions because body size, flexibility and preferred technique differ between climbers.
